target_moa.text: Omaveloxolone is postulated to activate the transcription factor Nrf2 (nuclear factor erythroid 2-like 2), which regulates the cellular response to oxidative stress and restores mitochondrial function, thereby restoring redox balance and reducing inflammation in FA, where Nrf2 signaling is impaired due to frataxin deficiency.

citations.quote: Omaveloxolone is proposed for the treatment of FA. The Applicant postulates that omaveloxolone activates the transcription factor nuclear factor (erythroid-derived 2)-like 2 (Nrf2), which regulates the cellular response to oxidative stress and restores mitochondrial function, thus restoring redox balance and reducing inflammation. The proposed dose is 150 mg by mouth daily on an empty stomach, one
The Applicant postulates that impairment of Nrf2 signaling associated with frataxin deficiency and mitochondrial dysfunction is involved in the pathogenesis and progression of FA.

citations.quote: Omaveloxolone (SKYCLARYS™) is a semi-synthetic oleanane triterpenoid compound that is proposed for the treatment of Friedreich's ataxia (FA).

key_safety.text: Generally well tolerated with no deaths in the controlled study. Most common adverse reactions (>=20% and greater than placebo): elevated liver enzymes AST/ALT (37% vs 2%), headache (37% vs 25%), nausea (33% vs 13%), abdominal pain (29% vs 6%), fatigue (24% vs 14%), diarrhea (20% vs 10%), musculoskeletal pain (20% vs 15%). Warnings: elevation of aminotransferases, elevation of BNP, and lipid abnormalities.

summary.text: Skyclarys (omaveloxolone) received traditional approval via a Priority review NDA for Friedreich's ataxia, supported by a single adequate and well-controlled study (Study 1402 Part 2) plus confirmatory evidence. It had orphan drug designation for FA (granted June 19, 2017), and the sponsor received a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher. The application was not referred to an advisory committee.
